claims.text: GDACS's Tropical Cyclone report for CHAMPI-26 (event id 1001338, episode 16, GLIDE TC-2026-000192-GUM) rates the storm an Overall Red alert (score 2.5), tracking Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands over a 14-18 October 2026 window, with an estimated 180,000 people exposed to Category 1 (120 km/h) or higher winds and a JTWC-sourced maximum sustained wind of 259 km/h. Vulnerability for Guam is rated medium.

NWS Tiyan Guam's active-alerts feed (api.weather.gov, checked 17 October 2026) lists a Typhoon Warning for Guam and Rota and a Typhoon Watch plus Tropical Storm Warning for Tinian and Saipan, issued 3:06 PM ChST: Typhoon Champi (29W) was about 225 miles east-southeast of Guam, moving west-northwest at 18 mph, forecast to pass just south of or over Guam as a Category 3 storm, likely Sunday morning. The feed also lists a Coastal Flood Warning and High Surf Warning (issued 4:31 PM ChST, surf to 35 feet on Guam, 20-25 feet on Rota, 15-20 feet on Tinian/Saipan, coastal inundation of 5-7 feet on Guam) and a Flood Watch (issued 4:10 PM ChST, forecast rainfall of 8-14 inches on Guam, 5-8 inches on Rota, 3-5 inches on Tinian/Saipan).

NWS Tiyan Guam's active-alerts feed (api.weather.gov, checked 18 October 2026, 7:05 PM ChST): a Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued 5:51 PM ChST states the Typhoon Warnings for Guam and Rota have been cancelled, instructing residents to stay in shelter until the all-clear. At the 5 PM ChST advisory, Typhoon Champi (29W) was centered near 13.0N 142.3E, about 170 miles west of Guam, moving west at 10 mph with maximum sustained winds near 150 mph (Super Typhoon strength), continuing to move away from Guam and the Marianas. Guam, Rota, Tinian and Saipan remain under a Wind Advisory (southeast winds 25-35 mph on Guam/Rota, 15-25 mph on Saipan/Tinian), a High Surf Advisory (9-14 ft surf) and Rip Current Statement, and a Flood Watch (forecast 1-4 inches of additional rain from outer rainbands), all through 4:00 AM ChST on 19 October. No deaths, injuries or damage have yet been confirmed by an authoritative source.

description: Typhoon Champi tracked through the western Pacific toward Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands, intensifying into a Super Typhoon with JTWC-sourced maximum sustained winds of 259 km/h (150 mph) as it made its closest approach on 18 October 2026. The storm's center passed about 170 miles west of Guam without a direct landfall, and the US National Weather Service cancelled its Typhoon Warnings for Guam and Rota that evening as Champi continued moving west, away from the islands. GDACS rates the storm an Overall Red alert, estimating about 180,000 people in Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands were exposed to Category 1 or higher winds. Guam, Rota, Tinian and Saipan remain under a Wind Advisory, High Surf Advisory, Rip Current Statement and Flood Watch into the morning of 19 October. No deaths, injuries or damage have yet been confirmed by an authoritative source.

impact.summary: GDACS's Red-alert report for Typhoon Champi estimates about 180,000 people in Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands exposed to Category 1 or higher winds, with JTWC-sourced maximum sustained winds reaching 259 km/h (150 mph, Super Typhoon strength). The storm's center passed about 170 miles west of Guam on 18 October without a direct landfall, and the National Weather Service cancelled its Typhoon Warnings for Guam and Rota that evening as Champi moved away to the west; a Wind Advisory, High Surf Advisory, Rip Current Statement and Flood Watch remain in effect for Guam, Rota, Tinian and Saipan into the morning of 19 October. No deaths, injuries or damage have yet been confirmed by an authoritative source.

name: Typhoon Champi — Guam & Northern Mariana Islands

updates.text: Champi reached Super Typhoon strength (259 km/h sustained winds) and passed about 170 miles west of Guam without a direct landfall; NWS cancelled its Typhoon Warnings for Guam and Rota the evening of 18 October as the storm moved away west. A Wind Advisory, High Surf Advisory and Flood Watch remain active into 19 October. No deaths or damage confirmed yet.
